title: How a Turbocharger Works in 60 Seconds 🌀🔥 #shorts
description:
A turbo spins up to around 150,000 times a minute using exhaust gas your engine would throw away. The exhaust drives a turbine, a shaft spins a compressor, and an intercooler cools the squeezed air so the engine can burn more fuel. Follow Inside 60 for a new "how it works" explained in 60 seconds.

#turbo #howitworks #shorts

steps.label: Wasted Heat
steps.text: A turbo can spin up to *150,000 times* a minute, powered by gas your engine throws away.

steps.label: Exhaust
steps.text: Hot *exhaust* gas rushes out of the engine and into the turbo.

steps.label: Turbine
steps.text: It blasts a *turbine* wheel and spins it incredibly fast.

steps.label: Compressor
steps.text: A shaft links it to a *compressor* wheel, which sucks in fresh air and squeezes it.

steps.label: Intercooler
steps.text: Squeezed air gets hot, so an *intercooler* cools it, packing in even more oxygen.

steps.label: More Power
steps.text: More air lets the engine burn more fuel, so a *small engine* makes big power.

steps.label: Recap
steps.text: Waste gas, more *power*. Follow Inside 60 for more.
